data.description:
## Why
After inspecting several workers, the operator needs to return to the tab actually read, and an agent needs a bounded, readable account of that navigation. Backlog item: W4; D20 explicitly makes agent-readable `c11 history` core 1.0.

## Evidence
- c11: `Sources/TabSeenClock.swift:6-38,138-171` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) defines real operator visibility, transition timestamps and persistence seeding. It is event-driven, not a per-keystroke sampler. C11-243 is already done and is the foundation, not a duplicate history ticket.
- c11: `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:1085-1088,3886-3957` holds a capped workspace-only back/forward history. `Sources/SocketHandlers/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:41-42` dispatches workspace.last. `Sources/SessionPersistence.swift:379-389` persists last_seen_at, not a navigation trail; `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:5690-5703` and `Sources/Workspace.swift:278-279` preserve workspace/tab UUIDs on restore.
- c11: `Sources/SessionPersistence.swift:524-535` has no durable window ID in its snapshot. Resolve restored window/area location from the live workspace/tab UUID rather than assuming every focus-context ID survives. `Sources/c11App.swift:1021-1030` binds browser Back/Forward to Cmd+[ and Cmd+].
- Upstream: cmux #4160/#8654/#9329 and #9296; `Packages/macOS/CmuxWorkspaces/Sources/CmuxWorkspaces/Navigation/FocusHistoryModel.swift` at upstream/main (920ff39ff7) supplies capped history, duplicate pruning and navigation-recording suppression patterns. Its raw-focus source is not c11's source.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §4a; Fable row 4.13; Astra rows 4.13/4.13b and §5 point 9 (UUID history does not depend on stable short ordinals). BACKLOG.md W4/D20 overrides the older if-time/agent-history deferral recommendations in `c11-1.0.html`. Its D16/D15 exclusions preserve browser shortcuts and exclude stable tab-number work.

## Scope
In: dwell-qualified seen history, bounded UUID persistence, `c11 history [--json] [--limit N]`, `c11 history back|forward`, rebindable navigation actions and compatibility for workspace.last. History is available to agents under the existing local socket access model.
Out: browser shortcut remapping (D16), stable tab numbers (D15), Recently Closed/reopening processes, account restore, a searchable history pane, journal/analytics implementation, screen-content classification and automatic task-priority inference. W1-W3 groups are not prerequisites. Do not reintroduce the older proposal to postpone agent readability.

## Approach
Feed a small, testable history model from TabSeenTracker visibility transitions, with an injectable clock and a documented tunable dwell threshold (proposal: about one second). Store workspace/tab UUID, seen time and dwell; use current window/area context to locate a moved/restored live target. Cap retention (proposal: 200 entries), prune closed targets, deduplicate consecutive visits and truncate forward history only for a new qualified visit. Back/forward traversal must not record itself and destroy its forward branch. Keep persistence off keystroke paths at the existing snapshot cadence, documenting the autosave loss window. Expose titles, current refs, UUIDs and dwell in JSON without transcript bodies. Add configurable actions without stealing existing browser chords, and update/sync the c11 skill/API reference.

## Acceptance criteria
1. With an injected clock and a one-second configured threshold, visits to A for two seconds, B for 0.2 seconds and C for two seconds retain A/C while skipping B. Repeated observations of the same tab do not multiply entries; cap/limit behavior and ordering are documented and tested.
2. Background socket focus changes, lock, screensaver and sleep do not generate visits or count unseen time toward dwell. A foreground socket change that genuinely changes the seen tab can qualify, matching C11-243's definition rather than guessing input provenance.
3. On a tagged build, dwell on A/B/C, go back to B and forward to C, then back to B and dwell on D. Forward C is discarded only for the new qualified visit; traversal itself preserves the branch. Closed targets are skipped; empty/boundary histories return a documented result. workspace.last retains its documented workspace-navigation behavior.
4. `c11 history --json --limit 2` returns at most two correctly ordered entries with target UUID/current ref, title, timestamp and dwell; readable output describes the same visits. Reading history changes neither focus nor seen data. Invalid limits return actionable errors. Back/forward are explicit in-app focus commands and never activate/raise the macOS app.
5. Save and restart a tagged fixture with terminal/browser/markdown targets; history resolves restored UUIDs even if short refs/window/area IDs change. Moving a tab resolves its current location; closing it prunes the dead target without reopening a process. Old snapshots with no history still restore.
6. Bind history navigation to available custom keys and drive it through the UI. Browser Cmd+[ / Cmd+] still navigate browser pages. No existing default chord is silently reassigned.
7. New UI/help strings are localized in all six locales, the skill examples match the commands, and the installed skill is synced. History stays within its documented cap and exposes no prompt/tool bodies or private transcript content.

## Validation
Extend the injectable seen-clock behavioral tests and snapshot/history fixtures; use tests_v2 on a tagged socket for JSON, traversal, dead targets and restart. A fresh-context computer-use pass proves dwell selection, custom keys, browser shortcut preservation and background-focus behavior. Compare navigation churn during typing against F2's baseline; build and soak on Atlas after F1/C11-216 using build locks and tagged QA launch. Do not use source-text tests or claim runtime verification from build-for-testing alone.

## Dependencies
C11-243 is the completed foundation, confirmed in origin/main; no reopening needed. F1 (C11-216) for build/soak execution; F2 for performance comparison. No dependency on D15, account restoration, W1-W3 or J2. The lead links cross-workstream dependencies.

## Risks
Dwell/navigation feedback can destroy forward history or inflate dwell through sleep. Avoid main-thread I/O and all per-key sampling. Persist minimal bounded attention metadata; do not treat history as consent or an instruction to agents. No tenant config writes. Localize six locales and keep public fixtures/screenshots synthetic. Snapshot cadence is not synchronous crash durability.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: observe operator-visible navigation and expose a local primitive; no agent hooks, tenant config changes or inferred task policy.

Plan SHA256 277cda2d0dfff0e0b9d818d64ead949529b3925f93c0887f50941101f94a659c. No open human decisions. Planning only: product code, builds, tests, runtime/UI proof, commits and pushes have not started. Await Orchestrator BUILD MODE; execution/validation remains Atlas-only.

Implementation is durable on branch c11-1.0/C11-262-focus-history. Base 86d45e218f220c89b592653de2f1c488d57068f7. Current HEAD 31949deadc99a6b69bfe5fda34152feffe4947d8.

Runtime harness review strengthened --window and background-focus oracles.

HEAD/pushed branch: 31949deadc99a6b69bfe5fda34152feffe4947d8 / c11-1.0/C11-262-focus-history. Base: 86d45e218f220c89b592653de2f1c488d57068f7.

Observed passing evidence:
1. Atlas targeted native test action: 48 tests, zero failures (31 FocusHistoryModelTests and 17 TabSeenClockTests), ** TEST SUCCEEDED **. Invocation f2a257159e774300b7ee7e11f91583b2, native test head c11a32b574a8a00358689e1d2b94ba2233783c2a. The only later commit strengthens tests_v2 runtime oracles; product and native-test sources are identical. Result/log/xcresult under build-remote/f2a257159e774300b7ee7e11f91583b2/.
2. Atlas packaged tagged Debug build passed at the handoff HEAD, clean source overlay. Invocation 20a6010bfdee4f6aa0b4d98f19ec7a69; result.json records source/submodule identity, compile=ok, tests=na, tag c11-262-history. Atlas executable SHA256 0b6f0540042f72d0d0073f849d500df48d3f43eebce0f3c046579100fd684576. Retrieved/ad-hoc-signed client executable SHA256 3de7c6e2c70e64aa5b2c60082c5b82b55a1d9bfc82fff48de3b75dfd9060dfd2.
3. CLI behavioral harness passed against that built CLI: C11_CLI_BIN=<tagged bundle>/Contents/Resources/bin/c11 python3 tests/test_cli_focus_history.py. Covers exact JSON and human output, authentication, list limits/arguments, navigation success/not_found, and absence of window.focus even with unrelated global --window.
4. Swift/Python syntax, project plist validity, English catalog jq validity, and git diff --check passed. These structural checks are separate from behavioral tests above.
5. Fresh-context static review found no production-code defects. Scoped review found and fixed selected-resume history loss and changed-threshold requalification; behavioral fixtures cover both. Runtime harness review strengthened the --window and background-focus selection oracles.

Architecture/privacy: only completed continuous being_seen visits qualify (1 s default, 200 cap). Persist workspace/tab UUIDs, visit start and dwell only. Resolve titles/types/live refs on read; no title, description, cwd, URL, transcript or conversation persistence. Closed UUIDs prune, moved UUIDs resolve live, and workspace.last stays on its separate unchanged stack. History list parses off-main with one bounded live snapshot on main; navigation uses the existing explicit in-app focus policy and activation suppression. No typing/hitTest/forceRefresh hooks or event-triggered disk writes. Existing 8 s autosave and termination save apply; open visits are absent from snapshots.

Runtime/UI proof is delegated to the batch Validator per the Orchestrator's explicit ruling: C11-262 is not on the pre-merge runtime risk list. An attempted second-serial Atlas guest was stopped after Setup Assistant blocked actual seen state and its Aqua session became unusable; no runtime acceptance pass is claimed from it. This ticket's guest was removed, and all other Tart guests are left alone. No further guest work. A tagged base control build also compiled (invocation cce5455cbd87465bbbd88e3eeba84c25 at base 86d45e218f); event-path/visual comparisons were not executed.

Validator scenario (batch Validator: own tagged build on Hyperion tonight, UI slot/display verification/time cap, QA fresh/resume):
1. Create synthetic terminal A/B/C/D. Foreground the tagged window and verify being_seen for A. Dwell A 2 s, B 0.2 s, C 2 s, then leave C. History retains A/C in order and skips B. Repeated current-tab observations do not add rows. Repeat a qualified visit for browser and markdown targets.
2. Complete A/B/C visits. Back to B, dwell; Forward to C, dwell; Back to B, dwell. Traversal keeps C's forward row. Dwell on a new D for 2 s and leave it: forward C is discarded. Empty/boundary navigation reports the documented not_found error. Close a historical target: its rows prune and navigation never reopens it. Move a live target between workspaces: history resolves its new workspace UUID/ref.
3. Run c11 history --json --limit 2 and readable history. Both describe the newest two completed visits, oldest to newest. Check full-stack position/counts and current marker; UUID/current refs/title/type/time/dwell are present, description/path/URL/transcript fields absent. Invalid limits fail with the documented error. Record focus and being_seen, then list with global --window naming a different window; neither changes.
4. Put Finder frontmost. Socket tab.focus changes do not record visits, even when left for 2 s. History Back/Forward must select their returned UUID in-app and leave Finder frontmost. Lock/screensaver/sleep/session inactivity interrupt dwell; overlapping reasons must remain interrupted until all clear. Two 0.4 s looks separated by an interruption must not combine.
5. Save/quit/relaunch with QA resume. Terminal/browser/markdown UUID history survives changed window/area/short refs and resolves the live locations. Close a target and save again: it stays pruned after restore. Resume-selected preserves history until live-target pruning. A raised dwell setting affects future visits, not saved rows; old snapshots with no history restore normally.
6. Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts initially shows None for both history actions. Record a confirmed-free chord (for example Cmd+Control+Option+Left after checking conflicts), synthesize it through the tagged UI, and verify selection changes. Delete clears the history binding and reset leaves it unbound. Recording Cmd+[ or Cmd+] on a history row is rejected; those chords still navigate browser pages. Capture menu/settings/browser screenshots.
7. Type into a focused terminal: the open visit stays absent and typing adds no history rows or event-triggered persistence writes. For comparison, use this tagged build and a tagged base/main build with the same navigation/typing scenario and record timings plus load averages; do not label handler turnaround as rendered keystroke latency. Inspect tree --no-layout for readable areas. Dismiss the tagged app with synthesized input and prove it closed.

Localization/skill landing: six English catalog/call-site keys added (shortcut.focusHistoryBack.label, shortcut.focusHistoryForward.label, shortcut.unbound, menu.history.title, menu.history.back, menu.history.forward). Six-locale translation is C11-291. Skill source/API documentation updated; only Merge Captain syncs installed copies from merged main. No installed skills edited/synced by this owner. No merge/release/deploy performed.

Verdict: **PASS** for static code review.

- Reviewed head: `31949deadc99a6b69bfe5fda34152feffe4947d8`.
- Merge-base: `86d45e218f220c89b592653de2f1c488d57068f7`.
- Current main checked: `7bb785741750ddeb8ab12b4cf6472593fb8c3550`.

## Blocking

None found in the complete 21-file diff and the unchanged selection, visibility, close, restore, shortcut, and socket-policy seams it touches.

Recording is attached to the existing seen-transition branch, after its unchanged-panel early return. Interrupted and background states therefore use the same visibility definition as last_seen_at. The model qualifies continuous dwell, caps retention at 200, suppresses traversal landings, preserves forward history on repeated current visits, and prunes closed UUIDs. Listing does not record visits or select targets; CLI history bypasses the global window-focus preamble. Navigation uses the existing explicit-focus socket policy. No new typing, TabItemView-body, telemetry, or event-triggered disk-write work was found.

Persistence adds an optional snapshot field without changing the schema version, preserves it through resume selection, and resolves live UUID locations after restore. Saved rows contain only workspace/tab UUIDs, seen time, and dwell; titles and refs are resolved live. No new tenant-config writes or private fixture content were found. The six new UI strings have localized call sites and English catalog entries; translations remain assigned to C11-291 under the accepted plan.

C11-259 is included in the review base. The newer C11-299 normalization copies the app snapshot and preserves its history field; C11-300's owned-workspace close path retains the existing forget/prune integration. Read-only three-way merge inspection against the main above produced no conflict markers, and GitHub reported MERGEABLE. This is static compatibility evidence, not a compiled integration result.

## Non-blocking

None.

## Evidence reviewed

Validation comment `ev_01M3XK6VX5CSFCE6VZN2SRWZ80` and its local Atlas result manifests/build logs were inspected. The native test log records 31 FocusHistoryModelTests plus 17 TabSeenClockTests, zero failures, and TEST SUCCEEDED at `c11a32b574a8a00358689e1d2b94ba2233783c2a`. Its only difference from the reviewed head is nine lines in the Python runtime harness; product and native-test sources are identical. The tagged Debug build manifest names the exact reviewed head, a clean overlay, compile success, and tests=na; its log records BUILD SUCCEEDED.

The built-CLI fake-socket harness pass is owner-reported in that validation comment. Its checked-in assertions exercise parsing, rendering, navigation errors, and absence of the window-focus preamble. The native and Python tests reviewed are behavioral. I did not run builds, tests, or the application. `git diff --check` passed and the detached checkout remained clean. The PR head was rechecked unchanged; build, compatibility, and other CI jobs were still queued. CI remains the Merge Captain's gate.

## Runtime proof still required

The accepted Orchestrator ruling explicitly delegates C11-262 runtime proof to the batch Validator and removes it from the pre-merge runtime risk list. Its absence is therefore not a blocker for this static-review verdict. No runtime acceptance pass is claimed here.

The Validator must execute the seven numbered scenarios in the validation comment: actual seen-state dwell and interruptions; back/forward branch preservation; non-focusing reads and background navigation; moved/closed targets; terminal/browser/markdown UUID restore; custom shortcut recording and browser chord preservation; and typing/navigation comparison against the tagged control. Use the authorized tagged validation environment specified by that ruling. Merge Captain must also sync the installed skill from merged main. These deferred checks, translation completion, and CI success are not implied by PASS.

Architecture/privacy: only completed continuous being_seen visits qualify (1 s default, 200 cap). Persist workspace/tab UUIDs, visit start and dwell only. Resolve titles/types/live refs on read; no title, description, cwd, URL, transcript or conversation persistence. Closed UUIDs prune, moved UUIDs resolve live, and workspace.last stays on its separate unchanged stack. History list parses off-main with one bounded live snapshot on main; navigation uses the existing explicit in-app focus policy and activation suppression. No typing/hitTest/forceRefresh hooks or event-triggered disk writes. Existing 8 s autosave and termination save apply; open visits are absent from snapshots.

Runtime/UI proof is delegated to the batch Validator per the Orchestrator's explicit ruling: C11-262 is not on the pre-merge runtime risk list. An attempted second-serial remote worker guest was stopped after Setup Assistant blocked actual seen state and its Aqua session became unusable; no runtime acceptance pass is claimed from it. This ticket's guest was removed, and all other Tart guests are left alone. No further guest work. A tagged base control build also compiled (invocation [run-id redacted] at base 86d45e218f); event-path/visual comparisons were not executed.

Validator scenario (batch Validator: own tagged build on local client tonight, UI slot/display verification/time cap, QA fresh/resume):
1. Create synthetic terminal A/B/C/D. Foreground the tagged window and verify being_seen for A. Dwell A 2 s, B 0.2 s, C 2 s, then leave C. History retains A/C in order and skips B. Repeated current-tab observations do not add rows. Repeat a qualified visit for browser and markdown targets.
2. Complete A/B/C visits. Back to B, dwell; Forward to C, dwell; Back to B, dwell. Traversal keeps C's forward row. Dwell on a new D for 2 s and leave it: forward C is discarded. Empty/boundary navigation reports the documented not_found error. Close a historical target: its rows prune and navigation never reopens it. Move a live target between workspaces: history resolves its new workspace UUID/ref.
3. Run c11 history --json --limit 2 and readable history. Both describe the newest two completed visits, oldest to newest. Check full-stack position/counts and current marker; UUID/current refs/title/type/time/dwell are present, description/path/URL/transcript fields absent. Invalid limits fail with the documented error. Record focus and being_seen, then list with global --window naming a different window; neither changes.
4. Put Finder frontmost. Socket tab.focus changes do not record visits, even when left for 2 s. History Back/Forward must select their returned UUID in-app and leave Finder frontmost. Lock/screensaver/sleep/session inactivity interrupt dwell; overlapping reasons must remain interrupted until all clear. Two 0.4 s looks separated by an interruption must not combine.
5. Save/quit/relaunch with QA resume. Terminal/browser/markdown UUID history survives changed window/area/short refs and resolves the live locations. Close a target and save again: it stays pruned after restore. Resume-selected preserves history until live-target pruning. A raised dwell setting affects future visits, not saved rows; old snapshots with no history restore normally.
6. Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts initially shows None for both history actions. Record a confirmed-free chord (for example Cmd+Control+Option+Left after checking conflicts), synthesize it through the tagged UI, and verify selection changes. Delete clears the history binding and reset leaves it unbound. Recording Cmd+[ or Cmd+] on a history row is rejected; those chords still navigate browser pages. Capture menu/settings/browser screenshots.
7. Type into a focused terminal: the open visit stays absent and typing adds no history rows or event-triggered persistence writes. For comparison, use this tagged build and a tagged base/main build with the same navigation/typing scenario and record timings plus load averages; do not label handler turnaround as rendered keystroke latency. Inspect tree --no-layout for readable areas. Dismiss the tagged app with synthesized input and prove it closed.

Localization/skill landing: six English catalog/call-site keys added (shortcut.focusHistoryBack.label, shortcut.focusHistoryForward.label, shortcut.unbound, menu.history.title, menu.history.back, menu.history.forward). Six-locale translation is C11-291. Skill source/API documentation updated; only Merge Captain syncs installed copies from merged main. No installed skills edited/synced by this owner. No merge/release/deploy performed.
